title: Chapter 7 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of Docker networking: default bridge, custom networks, DNS, port mapping, and network management!

questions.question: Which network driver is used by default when you start a container without specifying a network?
questions.explanation: The default network driver is `bridge`, and the network name is `bridge`.

questions.question: Containers on the default bridge network can resolve each other by name.
questions.explanation: The default bridge does not have embedded DNS. Only custom bridge networks provide automatic name resolution.

questions.question: What command lists all Docker networks on the host?
questions.explanation: `docker network ls` lists the networks. `docker network inspect` gives details on one.

questions.question: How do you create a custom bridge network named 'backend'?
questions.explanation: `docker network create <name>` creates a network with the default bridge driver.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of using a custom bridge network over the default bridge?
options: It provides automatic DNS resolution by container name
It allows containers to share the host network
questions.explanation: Custom bridge networks have a built‑in DNS server that resolves container names to IPs.

questions.question: The embedded DNS server in a custom network listens on IP `________` inside the container.
questions.explanation: Docker’s embedded DNS runs at 127.0.0.11 within each container attached to a custom network.

questions.question: When you map a port with `-p 8080:80`, what does the first number (8080) represent?
questions.explanation: The syntax is `host_port:container_port`. So 8080 is the port on the host machine.

questions.question: If you run a container with `-P`, Docker publishes all exposed ports to random host ports.
questions.explanation: `-P` (uppercase) publishes all ports listed in the image’s EXPOSE instructions to random high ports.

questions.question: Which command shows the port mapping for a running container named 'web'?
questions.explanation: `docker port <container>` displays the current port mappings.

questions.question: What does the `--network host` option do?
options: The container shares the host’s network namespace
Connects the container to all networks
questions.explanation: The container uses the host's network directly; no virtual network is created.

questions.question: Which network driver would you use to completely isolate a container from the network?
questions.explanation: The `none` driver gives the container no network interface except loopback.

questions.question: You have a container `app` on network `front`. How do you attach it also to network `back` without recreating it?
questions.explanation: `docker network connect` adds a running container to an existing network.

questions.question: What does `docker network prune` do?
options: Deletes all networks, even those in use
Removes all unused networks (no containers connected)
Reclaims IP addresses from all networks
questions.explanation: It removes networks that are not referenced by any container.

questions.question: Docker automatically configures iptables rules to enable port mapping.
questions.explanation: Docker manipulates iptables to create NAT rules for port publishing.

questions.question: If you bind a port to `127.0.0.1:8080:80`, what does it mean?
options: The container listens on localhost only
The host only forwards traffic from localhost to the container
The container is only reachable from inside the Docker network
questions.explanation: Binding to 127.0.0.1 limits the host port to the loopback interface, so remote hosts cannot access it.

questions.question: What information does `docker network inspect my-net` provide?
options: Subnet, gateway, connected containers and their IPs
questions.explanation: It returns a JSON document with all configuration details and attached containers.

questions.question: Why is the legacy `--link` option discouraged?
options: It doesn't work with custom networks
It is less flexible than DNS-based service discovery and has been deprecated
questions.explanation: `--link` provided environment variables and host entries; DNS on custom networks is simpler and more robust.

questions.question: Two containers on the same custom bridge network can communicate without any port mapping.
questions.explanation: Within a network, containers can talk to each other directly on any port; port mapping is only for traffic from outside the network.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `--subnet` option in `docker network create`?
options: To define a custom IP address range for the network
To restrict which ports can be mapped
questions.explanation: `--subnet` lets you specify the CIDR range for the network, overriding the default auto‑assigned range.

questions.question: Which command shows detailed information about all containers and their network settings?
questions.explanation: `docker inspect` includes a `NetworkSettings` section with IPs, gateways, and port mappings.

questions.question: To remove a specific network, you use `docker network ___ <name>`.
questions.explanation: `docker network rm <name>` removes a specific network. `prune` removes all unused.

questions.question: When using the `host` network driver, what happens to port mappings (`-p`)?
options: They are required to expose ports
They are ignored because the container uses the host network directly
questions.explanation: In host mode, the container is using the host’s interfaces, so port mapping is meaningless; the container’s ports are directly accessible on the host.
